Small electronic items, such as microwaves, toasters, and hair dryers, cannot be collected by the city. Please take them to the electronics recycling box at City Hall or to any participating electronics store. Large furniture can also be brought directly to the city recycling center on weekends without a reservation, but a fee is charged by weight.
translation: 市の廃棄物管理課にお電話いただきありがとうございます。ソファやベッドなどの大型家具は、予約制でのみ回収します。少なくとも1週間前までにオンラインまたは電話で回収を予約し、コンビニエンスストアで回収シールをお買い求めください。電子レンジ、トースター、ドライヤーなどの小型電子機器は、市では回収できません。市役所の電子機器リサイクルボックス、または協力している電器店にお持ちください。大型家具は、週末であれば予約なしで市のリサイクルセンターに直接持ち込むこともできますが、重さに応じて料金がかかります。

questions.question: What should you do with the sofa?
choices: Take it to the recycling center this weekend.
Book a pickup for next week.
Put it out with the regular trash.
Take it to an electronics store.
questions.explanation: 今週末に引っ越すので1週間前予約の回収には間に合わない。週末なら予約なしでリサイクルセンターに持ち込める。

title: Real-Life: Passport renewal
situation: Your passport expires in two months. You are going abroad on business in three weeks. You hear the following information at the passport office.
script: Narrator: To renew your passport, please submit the application form, your current passport, and one photo taken within the last six months. Standard processing takes about four weeks. If you need your passport sooner, you can apply for express processing, which takes five business days and costs an additional sixty dollars. To apply for express processing, you must show proof of travel, such as a flight booking. Please also note that many countries require your passport to be valid for at least six months from the date you enter the country.
translation: パスポートを更新するには、申請書、現在のパスポート、6か月以内に撮影した写真1枚を提出してください。通常の手続きには約4週間かかります。もっと早く必要な場合は特急手続きを申請でき、5営業日で、追加料金60ドルがかかります。特急手続きを申請するには、航空券の予約など渡航の証明を提示する必要があります。また、多くの国では入国日から少なくとも6か月間パスポートが有効であることが求められますのでご注意ください。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Apply for express processing with proof of your flight.
Wait until after your trip to renew.
questions.explanation: 出発は3週間後で通常手続き(4週間)では間に合わず、残り2か月のパスポートでは入国できない国が多い。航空券の予約を示して特急手続きを申請する。

title: Real-Life: Cooking class
situation: You want to join a cooking class to learn how to make Italian food. You are a vegetarian. You hear the following information from a cooking school.
script: Narrator: Here are our cooking classes for next month. On Monday evenings, we offer Italian Basics, where you'll learn to make fresh pasta with meat sauce. On Wednesday evenings, our Mediterranean Vegetables class covers dishes from Italy, Greece, and Spain, all made without meat or fish. On Saturdays, we have Japanese Home Cooking, which includes several vegetarian options. Each class costs forty dollars. If you have any food allergies or dietary restrictions, please let us know when you register, and our chefs will try to provide alternatives where possible.
translation: 来月の料理教室をご案内します。月曜の夜は「イタリアンの基本」で、生パスタとミートソースの作り方を学びます。水曜の夜の「地中海の野菜料理」では、イタリア、ギリシャ、スペインの料理を、すべて肉や魚を使わずに作ります。土曜日は「日本の家庭料理」で、ベジタリアン向けの料理もいくつかあります。各クラス40ドルです。食物アレルギーや食事制限がある場合は、登録時にお知らせください。シェフができる限り代わりの料理をご用意します。

questions.question: Which class should you take?
choices: Both the Monday and Wednesday classes.
questions.explanation: 水曜の地中海の野菜料理はイタリア料理を含み、肉や魚を使わないのでベジタリアンに最適。月曜はミートソース、土曜は日本料理。

title: Real-Life: Job application
situation: You want to apply for a sales position at a company. You have three years of sales experience but no university degree. You hear the following message from the company's human resources department.
script: Narrator: Thank you for your interest in working with us. We're currently hiring for two positions in sales. The Sales Manager position requires a university degree and at least five years of sales experience. The Sales Representative position requires at least two years of experience in sales or customer service, but no degree is required. Applications for both positions must be submitted through our website by the end of this month. Please include your résumé and a cover letter. Applicants who pass the first stage will be invited to an interview in early next month.
translation: 当社での就職にご関心をお寄せいただきありがとうございます。現在、営業職を2つ募集しています。営業マネージャー職には大学の学位と5年以上の営業経験が必要です。営業担当者職には営業または顧客対応の経験が2年以上必要ですが、学位は不要です。どちらの職への応募も、今月末までに当社ウェブサイトから提出してください。履歴書とカバーレターを添付してください。一次選考を通過した方は、来月上旬に面接にお招きします。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Apply online for the Sales Manager position.
Apply online for the Sales Representative position.
Wait until next month to apply.
questions.explanation: 営業経験3年で学位なしなので、学位不要で経験2年以上の営業担当者職に応募できる。マネージャー職は学位と5年の経験が必要。

title: Real-Life: Ferry schedule
situation: You are on an island and need to catch a train on the mainland that leaves at 4:30 p.m. The train station is a 20-minute walk from the ferry terminal on the mainland. It is now 2:00 p.m. You hear the following announcement.
script: Narrator: Attention, passengers. Due to strong winds, the 2:30 ferry to the mainland has been canceled. The next ferry will depart at 3:30 and arrive at 4:15. A high-speed boat is also available at 2:45, arriving at the mainland at 3:15, but it requires an additional fare of twenty dollars. Please note that the high-speed boat arrives at the north pier, which is about ten minutes by bus from the main ferry terminal. Buses from the north pier run every fifteen minutes and stop in front of the train station.
translation: 乗客の皆様にお知らせします。強風のため、2時30分発の本土行きフェリーは欠航となりました。次のフェリーは3時30分に出発し、4時15分に到着します。2時45分発の高速船もご利用いただけ、本土には3時15分に到着しますが、追加料金20ドルがかかります。なお、高速船は北桟橋に到着します。北桟橋はメインのフェリーターミナルからバスで約10分です。北桟橋からのバスは15分ごとに運行し、駅前に停車します。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Wait for the winds to calm down.
Take the high-speed boat and walk to the station.
Take the high-speed boat and then a bus.
questions.explanation: 3時30分のフェリーは4時15分着で、駅まで徒歩20分では4時30分に間に合わない。高速船で3時15分に着き、駅前に停まるバスに乗れば間に合う。北桟橋から歩くと遠い。

title: Real-Life: Internet problem
situation: Your home internet has stopped working. The lights on your router are blinking red. You call the internet provider and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Thank you for calling Netlink Customer Support. We are currently experiencing a service outage in the Eastwood and Riverside areas. Our engineers are working on the problem, and service is expected to return by six p.m. If you live in another area, please first try turning your router off and on again. If the lights on your router are green but you still can't connect, please check your computer's settings. If the lights are blinking red, there may be a problem with the cable connection. In that case, please press two to book a visit from a technician.
translation: ネットリンクのカスタマーサポートにお電話いただきありがとうございます。現在、イーストウッドとリバーサイドの地域で通信障害が発生しています。技術者が対応中で、午後6時までに復旧する見込みです。ほかの地域にお住まいの方は、まずルーターの電源を入れ直してください。ルーターのランプが緑なのに接続できない場合は、パソコンの設定をご確認ください。ランプが赤く点滅している場合は、ケーブルの接続に問題がある可能性があります。その場合は、2を押して技術者の訪問をご予約ください。

questions.question: You live in the Northfield area. What should you do?
choices: Wait until six p.m. for service to return.
Restart your router and then book a technician if needed.
Call back after the outage ends.
questions.explanation: 障害地域ではないので、まずルーターを再起動する。ランプが赤く点滅したままならケーブルの問題なので技術者を予約する。

title: Real-Life: Charity run
situation: You want to take part in a charity run with your 10-year-old daughter. Neither of you has run long distances before. You hear the following information.
script: Narrator: The annual City Charity Run will be held on May twelfth. There are three courses this year. The ten-kilometer course is for experienced runners aged sixteen and over. The five-kilometer course is open to anyone aged twelve and over. For families with younger children, we have a three-kilometer fun run, which can be walked or run, and children under twelve must be accompanied by an adult. The registration fee is twenty dollars for adults and ten dollars for children, and all money goes to the children's hospital. Registration closes on April thirtieth.
translation: 毎年恒例の市民チャリティーランが5月12日に開催されます。今年は3つのコースがあります。10キロコースは16歳以上の経験豊富なランナー向けです。5キロコースは12歳以上なら誰でも参加できます。小さな子どものいる家族向けには3キロのファンランがあり、歩いても走ってもかまいません。12歳未満の子どもは大人の同伴が必要です。参加費は大人20ドル、子ども10ドルで、すべて子ども病院に寄付されます。申し込みは4月30日に締め切ります。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Register together for the five-kilometer course.
Register your daughter alone for the fun run.
Register together for the three-kilometer fun run.
questions.explanation: 10歳の娘は5キロコース(12歳以上)に出られない。3キロのファンランなら大人同伴で一緒に参加できる。

title: Real-Life: Bank card
situation: You lost your bank card yesterday. You think you dropped it on the street. You call your bank and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Thank you for calling First City Bank. If your card has been lost or stolen, please press one immediately to stop the card. This service is available twenty-four hours a day. After the card has been stopped, you can order a new card online, and it will arrive by mail within seven days. If you need a card urgently, you can visit any of our branches with photo identification, and a temporary card will be issued on the spot. If you notice any unusual transactions on your account, please report them to our fraud department.
translation: ファースト・シティ銀行にお電話いただきありがとうございます。カードを紛失または盗難された場合は、すぐに1を押してカードを停止してください。このサービスは24時間ご利用いただけます。カードの停止後、オンラインで新しいカードを注文でき、7日以内に郵送で届きます。急ぎでカードが必要な場合は、写真付きの身分証明書を持ってどの支店にお越しいただいても、その場で仮カードを発行します。口座に不審な取引があれば、不正対策部門にご報告ください。

questions.question: What should you do first?
choices: Visit a branch for a temporary card.
Press one to stop the card.
questions.explanation: まず1を押してカードを停止する。新カードの注文や仮カードの発行は停止の後。

title: Real-Life: Hiking trail
situation: You are planning a hike with your friends tomorrow. You want a trail that takes less than four hours and has a view of the lake. You hear the following information at a visitor center.
script: Narrator: Here's some information about our hiking trails. The Summit Trail takes about six hours and offers the best views of the lake and surrounding mountains. The Forest Trail is an easy two-hour walk through the woods, but there is no view of the lake. The Ridge Trail takes about three hours and has several viewpoints overlooking the lake. However, part of the Ridge Trail is currently closed because of a landslide, so hikers must use the detour, which adds about one and a half hours. The Waterfall Trail takes three and a half hours and passes the lake shore at the halfway point.
translation: ハイキングコースについてご案内します。サミット・トレイルは約6時間で、湖と周りの山々の最高の景色が見られます。フォレスト・トレイルは森の中を歩く2時間の易しいコースですが、湖は見えません。リッジ・トレイルは約3時間で、湖を見渡す展望地点がいくつかあります。ただし、リッジ・トレイルの一部は土砂崩れのため現在閉鎖中で、迂回路を使う必要があり、約1時間半長くなります。ウォーターフォール・トレイルは3時間半で、中間地点で湖畔を通ります。

questions.question: Which trail should you take?
questions.explanation: リッジ・トレイルは迂回で約4時間半になる。4時間未満で湖が見えるのは3時間半で湖畔を通るウォーターフォール・トレイル。

title: Real-Life: Office printer
situation: You need to print 200 color copies of a brochure by noon today. It is now 9 a.m. You call the office services department and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Hello, this is Office Services. For printing jobs of under fifty pages, please use the printers on your own floor. For larger jobs, please submit your file through the company print portal. Black-and-white jobs are usually completed within two hours. Color jobs take at least one business day because they are sent to an outside printing company. If you need color printing urgently, please contact Mark in the design department, who can approve the use of the high-speed color printer on the fifth floor for urgent jobs.
translation: こちらはオフィスサービス課です。50ページ未満の印刷は、各フロアのプリンターをご利用ください。それより多い印刷は、社内の印刷ポータルからファイルを提出してください。白黒印刷は通常2時間以内に仕上がります。カラー印刷は外部の印刷会社に送るため、少なくとも1営業日かかります。急ぎでカラー印刷が必要な場合は、デザイン部のマークに連絡してください。急ぎの仕事には、5階の高速カラープリンターの使用を承認してもらえます。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Contact Mark in the design department.
Submit your file through the print portal.
Use the printer on your own floor.
Print the brochure in black and white.
questions.explanation: 大量のカラー印刷を正午までに必要としている。印刷ポータル経由のカラーは1営業日かかるので、マークに連絡して5階の高速カラープリンターの使用許可を得る。

title: Part 2 Set 1
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: When will the new printer be delivered?
Man: (A) It prints in color.
Man: (B) Sometime on Thursday morning.
Man: (C) Yes, I delivered it yesterday.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Who's in charge of the budget report?
Woman: (A) Mr. Tanaka from accounting.
Woman: (B) About five thousand dollars.
Woman: (C) In the top drawer.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Would you like me to book a taxi for you?
Man: (A) I read that book last week.
Man: (B) It cost about twenty dollars.
Man: (C) Thanks, but I'll take the train.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Where did you put the client files?
Woman: (A) They're on your desk.
Woman: (B) Around three o'clock.
Woman: (C) Yes, the clients were pleased.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Why was the meeting moved to Friday?
Man: (A) The director is out of town until then.
Man: (B) In the main conference room.
Man: (C) Yes, I'll meet him there.

questions.question: When will the new printer be delivered?
questions.explanation: 「新しいプリンターはいつ届きますか」。When に対し「木曜の午前中のどこかで」と時を答えるのが適切。It prints in color は printer からの連想、Yes, I delivered ... は疑問詞の質問に Yes で答えており、delivered の繰り返しによるひっかけ。

questions.question: Who's in charge of the budget report?
questions.explanation: 「予算報告書の担当は誰ですか」。Who に対し人物(経理部のタナカさん)を答えている。金額や場所は budget や report からの連想で、質問に答えていない。

questions.question: Would you like me to book a taxi for you?
choices: I read that book last week.
Thanks, but I'll take the train.
questions.explanation: 「タクシーを予約しましょうか」という申し出に「ありがとう、でも電車で行きます」と断っている。book(予約する/本)の音のひっかけと、taxi 代からの連想の金額は不適切。

questions.question: Where did you put the client files?
questions.explanation: 「顧客ファイルをどこに置きましたか」に「あなたの机の上です」と場所を答えている。時刻は When への答え、Yes で始まる応答は疑問詞の質問に合わない。

questions.question: Why was the meeting moved to Friday?
choices: The director is out of town until then.
questions.explanation: 「なぜ会議は金曜に移ったのですか」に「部長がそれまで出張中だから」と理由を述べている。場所の応答と、meet の音を使った Yes の応答は不適切。

title: Part 2 Set 2
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: How often do you visit the Chicago office?
Man: (A) It's on Michigan Avenue.
Man: (B) For about two hours.
Man: (C) About once a month.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Isn't the cafeteria closed for renovations?
Woman: (A) I'll have the soup, please.
Woman: (B) Only until next Monday.
Woman: (C) Close the window, please.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Should we hire a caterer or prepare the food ourselves?
Man: (A) A caterer would save us time.
Man: (B) Yes, we should.
Man: (C) The food was delicious.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: The quarterly sales figures look much better than expected.
Woman: (A) Yes, the new campaign really helped.
Woman: (B) I expected you at nine.
Woman: (C) Four times a year.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Can you show me how to use the new scheduling software?
Man: (A) The show starts at eight.
Man: (B) It's a new schedule.
Man: (C) Sure, I have some time after lunch.

questions.question: How often do you visit the Chicago office?
questions.explanation: How often は頻度を尋ねる。「月に1回くらい」が適切。所在地や所要時間(How long への答え)は不適切。

questions.question: Isn't the cafeteria closed for renovations?
questions.explanation: 「食堂は改装で閉まっていませんか」に「来週の月曜までだけです」と答え、閉まっていることを認めつつ期間を補足している。注文の言葉は cafeteria からの連想、Close the window は closed の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Should we hire a caterer or prepare the food ourselves?
choices: A caterer would save us time.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文。「ケータリング業者のほうが時間の節約になる」と一方を選んでいる。選択疑問文に Yes / No では答えられない。料理の感想は過去の話で、質問と合わない。

questions.question: The quarterly sales figures look much better than expected.
choices: Yes, the new campaign really helped.
questions.explanation: 「四半期の売上が予想よりずっと良い」という発言に「新しいキャンペーンが効いた」と応じている。expected の繰り返しと、quarterly からの連想(年4回)はひっかけ。

questions.question: Can you show me how to use the new scheduling software?
choices: Sure, I have some time after lunch.
questions.explanation: 「新しい予定管理ソフトの使い方を教えてくれますか」という依頼に「いいですよ、昼食後なら時間があります」と応じている。show、schedule の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 3
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: What time does the shuttle bus leave for the airport?
Man: (A) Terminal two, I think.
Man: (B) I'll leave it on the table.
Man: (C) Every thirty minutes starting at six.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Have you finished reviewing the contract?
Woman: (A) I'm still on the last page.
Woman: (B) The contractor arrived late.
Woman: (C) Yes, the view is wonderful.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Which hotel are the conference speakers staying at?
Man: (A) They spoke for an hour.
Man: (B) Yes, they're staying for the weekend.
Man: (C) The one across from the convention center.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Let's ask Maria to lead the training session.
Woman: (A) The train was delayed this morning.
Woman: (B) I asked for the session schedule.
Woman: (C) Good idea—she knows the system best.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Do you know if the parking lot is open on weekends?
Man: (A) About twenty spaces.
Man: (B) I'll check with security.
Man: (C) It's a weekly report.

questions.question: What time does the shuttle bus leave for the airport?
choices: I'll leave it on the table.
Every thirty minutes starting at six.
questions.explanation: 「空港行きのシャトルバスは何時に出ますか」に「6時から30分おき」と時刻で答えている。ターミナルは airport からの連想、leave の別の意味(置いていく)はひっかけ。

questions.question: Have you finished reviewing the contract?
choices: I'm still on the last page.
questions.explanation: 「契約書の確認は終わりましたか」に「まだ最後のページを読んでいます」と、まだ終わっていないことを伝えている。contractor、view(reviewing の一部)の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Which hotel are the conference speakers staying at?
choices: Yes, they're staying for the weekend.
The one across from the convention center.
questions.explanation: Which hotel に対し「コンベンションセンターの向かいのホテル」と特定している。spoke(speakers の音)や、Yes で始まる応答は質問に答えていない。

questions.question: Let's ask Maria to lead the training session.
choices: The train was delayed this morning.
I asked for the session schedule.
Good idea—she knows the system best.
questions.explanation: 「マリアに研修を担当してもらおう」という提案に「いい考えだ、彼女がシステムに一番詳しい」と賛成している。train(training の音)や asked、session の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Do you know if the parking lot is open on weekends?
questions.explanation: 「駐車場が週末に開いているか知っていますか」に「警備に確認します」と、知らないので調べると答えている。台数は How many への答え、weekly は weekends の音のひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 4
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: How much will it cost to repair the copier?
Man: (A) Make twenty copies, please.
Man: (B) It was repaired last year.
Man: (C) The technician hasn't given us an estimate yet.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Why don't we have lunch on the patio today?
Woman: (A) That sounds nice—the weather is perfect.
Woman: (B) Because I had a late breakfast.
Woman: (C) Table for four, please.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Are you going to the trade show in Berlin or in Paris?
Man: (A) Yes, I showed it to them.
Man: (B) By plane, probably.
Man: (C) Actually, neither—I have to stay here.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Who should I send the invoice to?
Woman: (A) Ms. Lopez in the billing department.
Woman: (B) By the end of the month.
Woman: (C) I sent the photos yesterday.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: The elevator on the east side is out of order again.
Man: (A) I'll call the maintenance office.
Man: (B) In alphabetical order.
Man: (C) On the fifth floor, I think.

questions.question: How much will it cost to repair the copier?
choices: The technician hasn't given us an estimate yet.
questions.explanation: 「コピー機の修理はいくらかかりますか」に「技術者からまだ見積もりをもらっていない」と、金額が分からないことを伝えている。copies、repaired の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Why don't we have lunch on the patio today?
choices: That sounds nice—the weather is perfect.
Because I had a late breakfast.
questions.explanation: Why don't we ...? は「〜しませんか」という提案。「いいですね、天気も最高です」と応じている。Because で理由を答えるのは Why の誤解によるひっかけ。注文の言葉は lunch からの連想。

questions.question: Are you going to the trade show in Berlin or in Paris?
choices: Yes, I showed it to them.
Actually, neither—I have to stay here.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文に「実はどちらにも行かない、ここに残らないといけない」と答えている。選択疑問文に Yes は不適切。交通手段は How への答え。

questions.question: Who should I send the invoice to?
choices: Ms. Lopez in the billing department.
By the end of the month.
questions.explanation: 「請求書は誰に送ればいいですか」に「請求担当部署のロペスさん」と人物を答えている。期限は When への答え、sent の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: The elevator on the east side is out of order again.
choices: On the fifth floor, I think.
questions.explanation: 「東側のエレベーターがまた故障している」という発言に「保守管理室に電話します」と対応を述べている。order の別の意味(順番)や、elevator からの連想の階数はひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 5
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: Where can I find extra toner cartridges?
Man: (A) Yes, I found it.
Man: (B) In the supply cabinet next to the kitchen.
Man: (C) About two weeks ago.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: You've worked with this supplier before, haven't you?
Woman: (A) The supply room is locked.
Woman: (B) Yes, for about three years.
Woman: (C) No, I'll work from home tomorrow.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: When is the deadline for the grant application?
Man: (A) It was extended to May tenth.
Man: (B) About five pages long.
Man: (C) Mr. Grant from marketing.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Could you take a look at my presentation slides?
Woman: (A) I'd be happy to, after this call.
Woman: (B) I'll take the stairs.
Woman: (C) He presented it last week.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Why is the store closing early tonight?
Man: (A) Until nine on weekdays.
Man: (B) It's close to the station.
Man: (C) There's a staff training session.

questions.question: Where can I find extra toner cartridges?
choices: In the supply cabinet next to the kitchen.
questions.explanation: 「予備のトナーカートリッジはどこにありますか」に「給湯室の隣の備品棚」と場所を答えている。疑問詞の質問に Yes は不適切。時期は When への答え。

questions.question: You've worked with this supplier before, haven't you?
choices: No, I'll work from home tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 付加疑問文「この納入業者と以前仕事をしたことがありますよね」に「はい、3年ほど」と答えている。supply、work の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: When is the deadline for the grant application?
choices: It was extended to May tenth.
questions.explanation: 「助成金の申請期限はいつですか」に「5月10日に延長された」と答えている。分量は How long への答え、Grant という人名は grant の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Could you take a look at my presentation slides?
choices: I'd be happy to, after this call.
questions.explanation: 「プレゼンのスライドを見てもらえますか」という依頼に「喜んで、この電話の後に」と応じている。take、presented の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Why is the store closing early tonight?
questions.explanation: 「なぜ今夜は早く閉店するのですか」に「スタッフ研修があるから」と理由を述べている。営業時間の応答や、close(近い)の音のひっかけは不適切。

title: Part 2 Set 6
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: How long does it take to get to the factory from here?
Man: (A) It's a long table.
Man: (B) About forty minutes by car.
Man: (C) They make auto parts.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Would you prefer a window seat or an aisle seat?
Woman: (A) Whichever is closer to the front.
Woman: (B) Yes, I would.
Woman: (C) I saw it in the window.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: I can't find the agenda for this afternoon's meeting.
Man: (A) No, I didn't meet him.
Man: (B) At two thirty.
Man: (C) I just e-mailed it to everyone.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Who approved the new travel policy?
Woman: (A) The board voted on it last week.
Woman: (B) To Singapore and Tokyo.
Woman: (C) I'd prefer to travel light.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Is there a pharmacy near the hotel?
Man: (A) Yes, I booked the hotel.
Man: (B) Take two tablets a day.
Man: (C) There's one on the next block.

questions.question: How long does it take to get to the factory from here?
questions.explanation: How long は所要時間を尋ねる。「車で40分ほど」が適切。long の繰り返しと、factory からの連想(自動車部品を作っている)はひっかけ。

questions.question: Would you prefer a window seat or an aisle seat?
choices: Whichever is closer to the front.
I saw it in the window.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文に「前のほうに近いほうならどちらでも」と答えている。選択疑問文に Yes は不適切。window の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: I can't find the agenda for this afternoon's meeting.
choices: I just e-mailed it to everyone.
questions.explanation: 「今日の午後の会議の議題が見つからない」という発言に「さっき全員にメールで送った」と応じている。meet の音のひっかけや、会議の時刻は発言への応答になっていない。

questions.question: Who approved the new travel policy?
choices: The board voted on it last week.
questions.explanation: 「新しい出張規程を承認したのは誰ですか」に「先週、取締役会が採決した」と答えている。行き先は travel からの連想、travel の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Is there a pharmacy near the hotel?
choices: There's one on the next block.
questions.explanation: 「ホテルの近くに薬局はありますか」に「次の区画に1軒あります」と答えている。hotel の繰り返しと、pharmacy からの連想(錠剤を1日2回)はひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 7
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: What did you think of the candidate we interviewed?
Man: (A) In the second interview room.
Man: (B) She seemed very well prepared.
Man: (C) Around ten applicants.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Shouldn't we update the price list before the sale?
Woman: (A) Yes, I'm working on it now.
Woman: (B) Twenty percent off everything.
Woman: (C) It was sold out.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Where's the nearest place to get coffee around here?
Man: (A) There's a café in the lobby.
Man: (B) Two sugars, please.
Man: (C) Yes, it's near here.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: We're running low on printer paper.
Woman: (A) He's running in the marathon.
Woman: (B) I'll order more this afternoon.
Woman: (C) The paper said it would rain.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Did Mr. Kim call back about the shipment?
Man: (A) The ship is very large.
Man: (B) Not yet, but he said he would by noon.
Man: (C) Please call me Ken.

questions.question: What did you think of the candidate we interviewed?
questions.explanation: 「面接した候補者をどう思いましたか」に「とても準備ができているようだった」と感想を述べている。場所や人数は質問に答えていない。

questions.question: Shouldn't we update the price list before the sale?
choices: Yes, I'm working on it now.
questions.explanation: 「セールの前に価格表を更新すべきでは」に「はい、今やっています」と答えている。割引率や sold out は sale からの連想。

questions.question: Where's the nearest place to get coffee around here?
choices: There's a café in the lobby.
questions.explanation: 「この辺りで一番近いコーヒーが飲める場所は」に「ロビーにカフェがあります」と答えている。砂糖の注文は coffee からの連想、疑問詞の質問に Yes は不適切。

questions.question: We're running low on printer paper.
choices: The paper said it would rain.
questions.explanation: 「プリンター用紙が少なくなってきた」という発言に「今日の午後に追加で注文します」と応じている。running、paper(新聞)の別の意味を使ったひっかけ。

questions.question: Did Mr. Kim call back about the shipment?
choices: Not yet, but he said he would by noon.
questions.explanation: 「キムさんから出荷の件で折り返し電話はありましたか」に「まだですが、昼までにすると言っていました」と答えている。ship、call の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 8
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: How many people signed up for the workshop?
Man: (A) Over fifty so far.
Man: (B) Sign here, please.
Man: (C) On the third floor.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Do you want to review the proposal now or after lunch?
Woman: (A) Yes, it's a good proposal.
Woman: (B) Let's do it now while it's quiet.
Woman: (C) I had a sandwich.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Why hasn't the website been updated?
Man: (A) Yes, on the home page.
Man: (B) The designer is still working on the new photos.
Man: (C) I updated my phone yesterday.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: The client wants to change the delivery date.
Woman: (A) Yes, it was delivered.
Woman: (B) Twenty dollars in change.
Woman: (C) Did she say what date works better?
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Who's going to pick up the visitors from the station?
Man: (A) The train leaves from platform three.
Man: (B) Kevin volunteered to do it.
Man: (C) Yes, they're visiting tomorrow.

questions.question: How many people signed up for the workshop?
questions.explanation: How many は数を尋ねる。「今のところ50人以上」が適切。sign の繰り返しや場所は質問に答えていない。

questions.question: Do you want to review the proposal now or after lunch?
choices: Let's do it now while it's quiet.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文に「静かなうちに今やりましょう」と一方を選んでいる。Yes は不適切、サンドイッチは lunch からの連想。

questions.question: Why hasn't the website been updated?
choices: The designer is still working on the new photos.
questions.explanation: 「なぜウェブサイトが更新されていないのですか」に「デザイナーがまだ新しい写真を作業中」と理由を述べている。Yes で始まる応答や、updated の繰り返しは不適切。

questions.question: The client wants to change the delivery date.
choices: Did she say what date works better?
questions.explanation: 「顧客が納品日を変更したがっている」という発言に「どの日が都合がいいか言っていましたか」と聞き返している。delivered、change(おつり)の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Who's going to pick up the visitors from the station?
choices: The train leaves from platform three.
questions.explanation: 「駅まで来客を迎えに行くのは誰ですか」に「ケビンが引き受けてくれた」と人物を答えている。station からの連想(ホーム)や、Yes で始まる応答は不適切。

questions.question: Which room is the orientation being held in?
choices: Room 204, at the end of the hall.
questions.explanation: 「オリエンテーションはどの部屋で行われますか」に「廊下の突き当たりの204号室」と答えている。対象者の説明や held と hold の音のひっかけは不適切。

questions.question: Can I get a refund if the jacket doesn't fit?
choices: Yes, within thirty days with the receipt.
questions.explanation: 「ジャケットが合わなかったら返金してもらえますか」に「はい、レシートがあれば30日以内なら」と答えている。fitting、fund(refund の一部)の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: When are you moving into your new office?
choices: As soon as the furniture arrives.
questions.explanation: 「新しいオフィスにいつ移りますか」に「家具が届いたらすぐに」と時を答えている。場所は Where への答え、movie は moving の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Haven't the tickets for the concert sold out?
choices: I'll take a ticket to Boston.
There are a few left in the back row.
questions.explanation: 「コンサートのチケットは売り切れていないのですか」に「後ろの列に少し残っています」と答えている。会場の場所や、ticket の別の意味(乗車券)は不適切。

questions.question: I think we should postpone the product launch.
choices: The post office closes at five.
questions.explanation: 「製品の発売を延期すべきだと思う」という意見に「賛成です、パッケージが間に合っていない」と応じている。lunch(launch の音)、post(postpone の一部)はひっかけ。

questions.question: How do I connect to the guest Wi-Fi?
choices: The password is posted by the front desk.
questions.explanation: 「ゲスト用 Wi-Fi にはどう接続すればいいですか」に「パスワードはフロントの横に貼ってあります」と方法を答えている。guests、connections の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Is the budget meeting today or tomorrow?
choices: It's been moved to next week.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文に「来週に移りました」とどちらでもない答えを返している。Yes は不適切、長さは How long への答え。

questions.question: Who left this umbrella in the lobby?
choices: I think it belongs to the courier.
questions.explanation: 「ロビーにこの傘を置いていったのは誰ですか」に「配達員のものだと思います」と答えている。雨は umbrella からの連想、left(左)の別の意味はひっかけ。

questions.question: Why don't you take tomorrow off?
choices: Because the flight took off late.
I have a deadline to meet.
questions.explanation: Why don't you ...? は「〜したらどうですか」という提案。「締め切りがあるので」と断っている。Because で答えるのは Why の誤解、take off の別の意味もひっかけ。

questions.question: Ms. Chen's flight has been delayed.
choices: Then let's start the meeting without her.
questions.explanation: 「チェンさんの便が遅れている」という発言に「それなら彼女抜きで会議を始めましょう」と応じている。delightful は delayed の音、座席の位置は flight からの連想。

questions.question: Where should I park for the job interview?

questions.question: Hasn't the shipment from Mexico arrived yet?
questions.explanation: 「メキシコからの荷物はまだ届いていないのですか」に「税関で止まっている」と答えている。Mexico の繰り返しや、customers(customs と似た音)はひっかけ。

questions.question: Would you mind closing the door?
questions.explanation: Would you mind ...? は「〜してもらえますか」という依頼。「いいですよ(まったく構いません)」と応じている。closer、closes の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: What's the best way to contact the editor?
questions.explanation: 「編集者に連絡を取るにはどうするのが一番いいですか」に「彼女はメールを好みます」と答えている。edition(editor と似た音)、contact の別の意味はひっかけ。

questions.question: Our team won the industry award this year.
choices: Two or three times a year.
questions.explanation: 「うちのチームが今年の業界賞を受賞した」という報告に「おめでとう、すばらしい知らせだ」と応じている。重さは award(トロフィー)からの連想、頻度は year の繰り返しによるひっかけ。

questions.question: Should I print the handouts in color or black and white?

questions.question: Who's responsible for ordering office supplies?

questions.question: Could you send me the updated schedule?

questions.question: Are you taking the early flight or the late one?

questions.question: How about holding the party at the riverside restaurant?

questions.question: Who's covering the reception desk while Amy is away?

questions.question: What's causing the delay in production?
choices: One of the machines broke down.
questions.explanation: 「生産の遅れの原因は何ですか」に「機械の1台が故障した」と原因を答えている。delayed、product の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 18
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: When can you send me the revised estimate?
Man: (A) It was revised twice.
Man: (B) By the end of the day.
Man: (C) I sent it to the wrong address.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Which bus goes to the convention center?
Woman: (A) Number 15 stops right in front of it.
Woman: (B) About an hour.
Woman: (C) Yes, it's very convenient.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Don't you need to renew your passport?
Man: (A) I already did it last month.
Man: (B) The news starts at six.
Man: (C) Pass me the salt, please.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Would you like some help carrying those boxes?
Woman: (A) Thanks, that would be great.
Woman: (B) They're made of cardboard.
Woman: (C) I carry my own bag.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: The printer on the second floor is jammed again.
Man: (A) I like strawberry jam.
Man: (B) Two floors up.
Man: (C) Let's use the one downstairs for now.

questions.question: When can you send me the revised estimate?
choices: By the end of the day.
I sent it to the wrong address.
questions.explanation: 「修正した見積もりはいつ送れますか」に「今日中に」と時を答えている。revised の繰り返しや、過去に送った話は質問に合わない。

questions.question: Which bus goes to the convention center?
choices: Number 15 stops right in front of it.
questions.explanation: 「コンベンションセンターに行くのはどのバスですか」に「15番が目の前に止まります」と答えている。所要時間は How long への答え、convenient は convention の音。

questions.question: Don't you need to renew your passport?
choices: I already did it last month.
questions.explanation: 「パスポートを更新しなくていいのですか」に「先月もう済ませました」と答えている。news は renew の音、pass は passport の一部の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Would you like some help carrying those boxes?
questions.explanation: 「その箱を運ぶのを手伝いましょうか」という申し出に「ありがとう、助かります」と受けている。箱の素材の説明や、carry の繰り返しは申し出への応答になっていない。

questions.question: The printer on the second floor is jammed again.
choices: Let's use the one downstairs for now.
questions.explanation: 「2階のプリンターがまた詰まっている」という発言に「とりあえず下の階のを使おう」と応じている。jam(ジャム)の別の意味、floor からの連想はひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 19
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: Who's taking notes at today's meeting?
Man: (A) I think it's Mark's turn.
Man: (B) Notebooks are in the cabinet.
Man: (C) At three in the afternoon.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Why don't we ask for a bigger budget next year?
Woman: (A) I doubt management would approve it.
Woman: (B) Because it was too big.
Woman: (C) Next year in April.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Where did you buy that briefcase?
Man: (A) About a year ago.
Man: (B) In case it rains.
Man: (C) At the department store downtown.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Has the new intern started yet?
Woman: (A) She starts on Monday.
Woman: (B) The internet is down.
Woman: (C) Start the car, please.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Do you prefer working in the morning or the evening?
Man: (A) Yes, I work here.
Man: (B) I focus best early in the day.
Man: (C) Good evening, everyone.

questions.question: Who's taking notes at today's meeting?
questions.explanation: 「今日の会議の記録係は誰ですか」に「マークの番だと思う」と人物を答えている。notebooks は notes の音、時刻は When への答え。

questions.question: Why don't we ask for a bigger budget next year?
choices: I doubt management would approve it.
questions.explanation: Why don't we ...? は提案。「経営陣が承認するとは思えない」と懸念を述べている。Because で答えるのは Why の誤解、時期の答えは提案への応答になっていない。

questions.question: Where did you buy that briefcase?
questions.explanation: 「そのブリーフケースはどこで買いましたか」に「繁華街のデパートで」と場所を答えている。時期は When への答え、case の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Has the new intern started yet?
questions.explanation: 「新しいインターンはもう働き始めましたか」に「月曜から始まります」と答えている。internet は intern の音、start の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Do you prefer working in the morning or the evening?
choices: I focus best early in the day.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文に「朝早いほうが一番集中できる」と午前を選んでいる。Yes は不適切、evening の繰り返しはひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 20
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: How many copies of the brochure should I print?
Man: (A) It's on page five.
Man: (B) Yes, I'll copy it.
Man: (C) Two hundred should be enough.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Isn't the store manager on vacation this week?
Woman: (A) Store it in a cool place.
Woman: (B) She came back yesterday.
Woman: (C) I manage the sales team.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Where should we put the new sofa?
Man: (A) It's very comfortable.
Man: (B) Next to the window would be nice.
Man: (C) So far, so good.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: The marketing team needs the survey results by Friday.
Woman: (A) I'll have them ready by Thursday.
Woman: (B) Yes, I'm on the team.
Woman: (C) The market opens at nine.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: What did the customer complain about?
Man: (A) Customer service is on line two.
Man: (B) About twenty minutes ago.
Man: (C) The package arrived damaged.

questions.question: How many copies of the brochure should I print?
questions.explanation: 「パンフレットを何部印刷すればいいですか」に「200部で足りるはず」と数を答えている。ページの位置や、Yes で始まる応答は質問に合わない。

questions.question: Isn't the store manager on vacation this week?
choices: Store it in a cool place.
questions.explanation: 「店長は今週休暇中ではないのですか」に「昨日戻ってきました」と答えている。store(保管する)、manage の音の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Where should we put the new sofa?
choices: Next to the window would be nice.
questions.explanation: 「新しいソファをどこに置きましょうか」に「窓の隣がいいですね」と場所を答えている。座り心地の感想は質問に答えておらず、so は sofa の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: The marketing team needs the survey results by Friday.
choices: I'll have them ready by Thursday.
questions.explanation: 「マーケティングチームが金曜までに調査結果を必要としている」という発言に「木曜までに用意します」と応じている。team の繰り返し、market は marketing の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: What did the customer complain about?
choices: Customer service is on line two.
questions.explanation: 「顧客は何について苦情を言ったのですか」に「荷物が破損して届いた」と内容を答えている。customer の繰り返しや、時期の答えは質問に合わない。

title: A broken laptop
script:
Man: Linda, my laptop suddenly stopped working, and my report is due tomorrow.
Woman: Did you save the file anywhere else?
Man: I think it's backed up online automatically, but I've never checked.
Woman: Then use the computer in the library and log in to your account. If the file's there, you can finish it tonight and get the laptop repaired later.
Man: Good idea. I'll go there right after lunch.
translation:
男性:リンダ、ノートパソコンが急に動かなくなって、レポートの締め切りが明日なんだ。
女性:ファイルをほかのどこかに保存した?
男性:自動でオンラインにバックアップされていると思うけど、確かめたことはないんだ。
女性:それなら図書館のパソコンで自分のアカウントにログインして。ファイルがあれば今夜仕上げて、パソコンの修理は後でいいわよ。
男性:いい考えだね。昼食の後すぐに行くよ。

questions.question: What will the man do first?
choices: Check for his file on a library computer.
Take his laptop to a repair shop.
Ask his teacher for more time.
questions.explanation: 女性の提案に従い、昼食後すぐ図書館のパソコンでファイルを確認する。修理は後回しで、期限の延長や購入の話は出ていない。

title: Choosing a gym
script:
Woman: I've decided to join a gym, but I can't decide between the one near my office and the one near home.
Man: Which one is cheaper?
Woman: The one near my office, but I'd have to go before work, and I'm terrible at waking up early.
Man: Then the one near home makes more sense. You're more likely to keep going if it fits your routine.
Woman: You're right. Paying a little more is better than wasting money on a gym I never use.
translation:
女性:ジムに入ることにしたんだけど、職場の近くと家の近くのどちらにするか決められないの。
男性:どっちが安いの?
女性:職場の近くのほう。でも仕事の前に行かないといけなくて、私は早起きが本当に苦手なの。
男性:それなら家の近くのほうが理にかなっているよ。生活習慣に合っているほうが続けやすいから。
女性:そうね。使わないジムにお金を無駄にするより、少し多く払うほうがいいわ。

questions.question: What will the woman probably do?
choices: Join the cheaper gym near her office.
Join the gym near her home.
Start getting up earlier every day.
Exercise at home instead of joining a gym.
questions.explanation: 早起きが苦手なので、少し高くても続けやすい家の近くのジムが良いと納得している。

title: A dinner reservation
script:
Man: Hello, I'd like to book a table for six people this Friday at seven.
Woman: I'm sorry, we're fully booked at seven. We have a table at eight thirty, or we could seat you at seven on our outdoor terrace.
Man: Hmm, it's supposed to be cold on Friday, and some of my guests are elderly.
Woman: I understand. Would you like the later time, then?
Man: Yes, please. I'll let everyone know.
translation:
男性:もしもし、今週の金曜7時に6人で予約したいのですが。
女性:申し訳ありません、7時は満席です。8時半ならお席がございます。または7時にテラス席をご用意できます。
男性:うーん、金曜は寒くなるらしいし、高齢の客もいるんです。
女性:承知しました。では遅い時間になさいますか。
男性:はい、お願いします。みんなに知らせます。

questions.question: What does the man decide to do?
choices: Sit on the outdoor terrace at seven.
Book a table inside at eight thirty.
Change the reservation to another day.
questions.explanation: 寒さと高齢の客を理由にテラス席を避け、遅い時間(8時半)の予約にしている。

title: A volunteer opportunity
script:
Woman: Jake, the community center is looking for volunteers to teach computer skills to seniors.
Man: That sounds interesting, but I work until six on weekdays.
Woman: The classes are on Saturday mornings.
Man: Oh, then I could do it. I'm not a professional, though. Do they provide any training?
Woman: There's a short session for new volunteers next week. I'll send you the details.
Man: Thanks. I'll sign up for that first.
translation:
女性:ジェイク、コミュニティセンターが高齢者にパソコンを教えるボランティアを探しているわ。
男性:面白そうだけど、平日は6時まで仕事なんだ。
女性:教室は土曜の午前よ。
男性:それならできるよ。でも専門家じゃないんだ。研修はあるのかな。
女性:来週、新しいボランティア向けの短い説明会があるわ。詳しいことを送るね。
男性:ありがとう。まずそれに申し込むよ。

questions.question: What will the man do next?
choices: Ask his boss for weekdays off.
Sign up for a training session.
questions.explanation: 最後に「まずそれ(新しいボランティア向けの説明会)に申し込む」と言っている。

title: Moving apartments
script:
Man: How's the apartment hunting going, Emma?
Woman: Not great. The places near the station are too expensive, and the cheaper ones are a forty-minute bus ride away.
Man: Have you thought about sharing a place? My cousin is looking for a roommate, and her apartment is only ten minutes from the station.
Woman: Really? I've never lived with anyone before, but it might be worth meeting her.
Man: I'll give her your number.
translation:
男性:エマ、部屋探しはどう?
女性:あまりうまくいってないの。駅の近くは高すぎるし、安い所はバスで40分かかるの。
男性:ルームシェアは考えた?いとこがルームメイトを探していて、彼女の部屋は駅から10分なんだ。
女性:本当?誰かと住んだことはないけど、会ってみる価値はあるかもね。
男性:君の番号を彼女に伝えておくよ。

questions.question: What is the woman's problem?
choices: She cannot find an affordable apartment in a convenient location.
She does not get along with her current roommate.
Her apartment is too far from her office.
She has to move out of her apartment by next week.
questions.explanation: 駅の近くは高すぎ、安い所は遠いと言っている。手頃で便利な部屋が見つからないことが問題。

title: A presentation
script:
Woman: Tom, could you look over my presentation slides before tomorrow's meeting?
Man: Sure. Hmm, there's a lot of text on each slide. People might stop listening and just read.
Woman: I was worried I'd forget what to say.
Man: Put the details in your speaker notes instead, and keep only the key points and charts on the slides.
Woman: OK, I'll change them tonight and practice a few times.
translation:
女性:トム、明日の会議の前にプレゼンのスライドを見てくれる?
男性:いいよ。うーん、どのスライドも文字が多いね。みんな話を聞かずに読むだけになるかも。
女性:言うことを忘れそうで心配だったの。
男性:詳しい内容は発表者用のメモに書いて、スライドには要点とグラフだけを残したら。
女性:わかった、今夜直して何回か練習するわ。

questions.question: What does the man suggest?
choices: Adding more charts to the speaker notes.
Reducing the amount of text on the slides.
Reading the slides aloud during the meeting.
questions.explanation: 文字が多すぎるので、詳細は発表者用メモに移しスライドには要点とグラフだけ残すよう提案している。

title: Lost luggage
script:
Man: Excuse me, my suitcase didn't come out at baggage claim.
Woman: I'm sorry about that. Could you show me your baggage tag? ... It looks like your bag was put on a different flight. It should arrive here tomorrow morning.
Man: But I'm leaving for a conference in another city early tomorrow.
Woman: In that case, we can deliver it directly to your hotel there. Please write the address on this form.
translation:
男性:すみません、手荷物受取所でスーツケースが出てこなかったんです。
女性:申し訳ございません。手荷物タグを見せていただけますか。……お荷物は別の便に載せられたようです。明朝こちらに着くはずです。
男性:でも明日の朝早く、別の都市の会議に出発するんです。
女性:その場合は、そちらのホテルに直接お届けできます。この用紙に住所をご記入ください。

questions.question: What will probably happen to the man's suitcase?
choices: It will be sent to his hotel in another city.
He will pick it up at the airport tomorrow.
It will be returned to the airport he left from.
It will arrive on his flight tonight.
questions.explanation: 男性が明朝別の都市へ発つので、係員はそちらのホテルに直接届けると言い、住所を書くよう頼んでいる。

title: A birthday gift
script:
Woman: Dad's birthday is next week. Any ideas for a present?
Man: He's been talking about starting a vegetable garden since he retired.
Woman: Oh, we could buy him some gardening tools.
Man: He already has a whole box of them from Grandpa. What about a gardening class at the community center? He'd meet people, too.
Woman: That's perfect. He's been saying he's bored at home. I'll check the schedule.
translation:
女性:お父さんの誕生日が来週ね。プレゼントの案はある?
男性:退職してから家庭菜園を始めたいって言っているよ。
女性:じゃあ園芸用品を買ってあげようか。
男性:おじいちゃんからもらった道具がひと箱あるんだ。コミュニティセンターの園芸教室はどう?人とも知り合えるし。
女性:ぴったりね。家にいて退屈だって言っていたもの。日程を調べてみるわ。

questions.question: What will they probably give their father?
questions.explanation: 道具はすでにあるので、人とも知り合える園芸教室にすることで意見がまとまった。

title: Working overtime
script:
Man: You look exhausted, Sarah. Have you been working late again?
Woman: Every night this week. My manager keeps giving me new projects.
Man: Have you told him how much you already have?
Woman: Not really. I don't want him to think I can't handle it.
Man: But if you don't tell him, he won't know. Why not show him a list of your current tasks and ask which ones are the priority?
Woman: I guess that's reasonable. I'll talk to him tomorrow.
translation:
男性:サラ、疲れきっているね。また遅くまで働いていたの?
女性:今週は毎晩よ。上司が次々に新しい仕事をくれるの。
男性:もうどれだけ抱えているか伝えた?
女性:あまり。こなせないと思われたくないの。
男性:でも言わなければ上司にはわからないよ。今の仕事のリストを見せて、どれを優先すべきか聞いたら?
女性:それは筋が通っているわね。明日話してみる。

questions.question: What will the woman do tomorrow?
choices: Ask a coworker to help with her projects.
Take a day off to rest.
Discuss her workload with her manager.
questions.explanation: 男性の提案を受け、今の仕事のリストを見せて優先順位を相談するために明日上司と話すと言っている。

title: A concert ticket
script:
Woman: Did you get tickets for the jazz concert?
Man: No, they sold out in ten minutes. Some people are reselling them online for three times the price.
Woman: I wouldn't pay that much. I heard the band is adding another show next month, though.
Man: Really? When do tickets go on sale?
Woman: This Friday at noon, I think.
Man: I'll set an alarm so I don't miss it.
translation:
女性:ジャズコンサートのチケットは取れた?
男性:いや、10分で売り切れたよ。ネットで3倍の値段で転売している人もいる。
女性:私ならそんなに払わないわ。でもバンドが来月追加公演をするって聞いたわよ。
男性:本当?チケットはいつ発売?
女性:今週の金曜の正午だと思う。
男性:逃さないようにアラームをかけておくよ。

questions.question: What will the man probably do?
choices: Go to the concert without a ticket.
Ask the woman to buy a ticket for him.
Try to buy a ticket for the extra show on Friday.
questions.explanation: 追加公演のチケットが金曜正午に発売されると聞き、逃さないようアラームをかけると言っている。転売品は高すぎるという流れ。

title: A noisy neighbor
script:
Man: The people upstairs were playing loud music until two in the morning again.
Woman: That's terrible. Have you talked to them?
Man: I left a note last week, but nothing changed.
Woman: Maybe you should contact the building manager. They can remind everyone about the rules for noise at night.
Man: I didn't want to make a big deal out of it, but I suppose I have no choice. I'll call the office this afternoon.
translation:
男性:上の階の人たちがまた夜中の2時まで大音量で音楽をかけていたんだ。
女性:ひどいわね。話はしたの?
男性:先週メモを置いたけど、何も変わらなかった。
女性:管理会社に連絡したほうがいいかも。夜の騒音のルールを全員に注意してくれるわ。
男性:大ごとにしたくなかったけど、仕方ないね。今日の午後、事務所に電話するよ。

questions.question: What will the man do this afternoon?
choices: Leave another note for his neighbors.
Start looking for a new apartment.
questions.explanation: メモでは効果がなかったので、今日の午後に管理事務所へ電話すると言っている。

title: A cooking mistake
script:
Woman: Something smells like it's burning!
Man: Oh no, the curry! I was on the phone and forgot about it.
Woman: Is any of it OK?
Man: The top part might be, but the bottom is completely burned. And our guests are coming in thirty minutes.
Woman: Don't worry. There's a good Indian restaurant around the corner that does takeout. I'll call and order now while you clean up.
Man: Thanks. You're a lifesaver.
translation:
女性:何か焦げているにおいがする!
男性:しまった、カレーだ!電話していて忘れていた。
女性:少しは大丈夫?
男性:上のほうは平気かもしれないけど、底は完全に焦げてる。しかもお客さんが30分後に来るんだ。
女性:心配しないで。角においしいインド料理店があって持ち帰りができるの。あなたが片付けている間に電話して注文するわ。
男性:ありがとう。助かるよ。

questions.question: What will the woman do?
choices: Ask the guests to come later.
Order takeout food from a restaurant.
questions.explanation: 近くのインド料理店に電話して持ち帰りを注文すると言っている。

title: Studying for an exam
script:
Man: I can't concentrate at home. My little brother is always playing video games in the living room.
Woman: Why don't you study at the city library? It's quiet, and it's open until nine.
Man: I tried, but all the seats were taken by the time I got there after school.
Woman: Our school's study room is open until seven on weekdays. Hardly anyone uses it.
Man: I didn't know that. I'll stay there after class from now on.
translation:
男性:家だと集中できないんだ。弟がいつも居間でゲームをしているから。
女性:市立図書館で勉強したら?静かだし9時まで開いているわよ。
男性:行ってみたけど、放課後に着いたころには席が全部埋まっていたんだ。
女性:学校の自習室は平日7時まで開いているわ。ほとんど誰も使っていないの。
男性:知らなかった。これからは授業の後そこに残るよ。

questions.question: Where will the boy probably study from now on?
choices: In the living room at home.
questions.explanation: 図書館は満席だったので、空いている学校の自習室に授業後残ると言っている。

title: A flight delay
script:
Woman: Our flight has been delayed by three hours. We're going to miss our connection in Chicago.
Man: Let's go to the airline counter. Maybe they can put us on a different route.
Woman: The line is huge. It'll take an hour at least.
Man: Then let's try the airline's app. Sometimes you can rebook there without waiting.
Woman: Good thinking. Oh, look—there's a direct flight this evening with two seats left.
Man: Book it before they're gone!
translation:
女性:私たちの便が3時間遅れるって。シカゴでの乗り継ぎに間に合わないわ。
男性:航空会社のカウンターに行こう。別の経路にしてくれるかもしれない。
女性:すごい行列よ。少なくとも1時間はかかるわ。
男性:じゃあ航空会社のアプリを試そう。待たずに予約変更できることがあるんだ。
女性:いい考えね。あ、見て、今夜の直行便に2席残っているわ。
男性:なくなる前に予約して!

questions.question: How will they probably travel?
choices: On a direct flight this evening.
On their original flight with a connection in Chicago.
On a flight booked at the airline counter.
By train instead of by plane.
questions.explanation: アプリで今夜の直行便に2席残っているのを見つけ、すぐ予約するよう言っている。

title: A team dinner
script:
Man: Kate, are you organizing the team dinner for Mr. Lee's retirement?
Woman: Yes, but I'm having trouble finding a date that works for everyone.
Man: Why not send an online poll with a few possible dates? Then people can just choose the days they're free.
Woman: That's much easier than emailing everyone individually. I'll set one up today.
Man: And let me know if you need help booking the restaurant.
translation:
男性:ケイト、リーさんの退職を祝うチームの食事会を準備しているの?
女性:ええ、でも全員の都合が合う日がなかなか見つからなくて。
男性:候補日をいくつか入れたオンライン投票を送ったら?そうすればみんな空いている日を選ぶだけで済むよ。
女性:一人ずつメールするよりずっと楽ね。今日作ってみるわ。
男性:店の予約に手伝いが必要なら言ってね。

questions.question: What will the woman do today?
choices: Book a restaurant for the dinner.
Create an online poll to choose a date.
Ask Mr. Lee which date he prefers.
questions.explanation: 男性の提案を受け、日程を決めるオンライン投票を今日作ると言っている。

title: Sleep and teenagers
script: Narrator: Many teenagers find it difficult to wake up early for school. Scientists say that this is not simply laziness. During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts, so teenagers naturally feel sleepy later at night. As a result, some schools in the United States have moved their start times from around seven thirty to after eight thirty. Studies found that students at these schools slept longer, were absent less often, and had better grades. However, some parents complained that later start times made it harder to arrange transportation and after-school activities.
translation: 多くの10代の若者は、学校のために早起きするのが難しいと感じている。科学者によれば、これは単なる怠けではない。思春期には体内時計がずれるため、10代は自然と夜遅くに眠くなる。その結果、米国の一部の学校は始業時間を7時半ごろから8時半以降に遅らせた。研究によると、こうした学校の生徒は睡眠時間が長くなり、欠席が減り、成績も上がった。しかし、始業が遅いと送迎や放課後の活動の調整が難しくなると不満を言う保護者もいた。

questions.question: Why do teenagers find it hard to wake up early?
choices: Their internal clocks shift during adolescence.
They spend too much time using smartphones.
They do not get enough exercise.
Their schools start later than before.
questions.explanation: 思春期には体内時計がずれて自然と夜遅くに眠くなる、と説明されている。単なる怠けではないとも述べている。

questions.question: What was one problem with later school start times?
choices: Some parents found transportation harder to arrange.
Teachers had to work longer hours.
questions.explanation: 最後に、送迎や放課後の活動の調整が難しくなると不満を言う保護者がいたとある。成績や欠席はむしろ改善した。

title: Cargo ships with sails
script: Narrator: Shipping is responsible for about three percent of global greenhouse gas emissions. To reduce this, some companies are returning to an old technology: sails. Modern cargo ships are being fitted with large, hard sails or spinning metal cylinders that use the wind to push the ship forward. Tests have shown that these devices can cut fuel use by up to twenty percent on some routes. However, the sails are expensive to install, and they work best on routes with strong, steady winds, so they cannot completely replace engines.
translation: 海運は世界の温室効果ガス排出量の約3%を占めている。これを減らすため、昔の技術である帆に立ち返る企業がある。現代の貨物船に、風を使って船を前に進める大きく硬い帆や回転する金属の円筒が取り付けられている。試験では、航路によっては燃料の使用を最大20%減らせることが示された。しかし帆は取り付け費用が高く、強く安定した風が吹く航路で最も効果を発揮するため、エンジンに完全に取って代わることはできない。

questions.question: What have tests shown about the new sails?
choices: They allow ships to travel twice as fast.
They work best when there is no wind.
They can reduce fuel use on some routes.
They have replaced engines on most ships.
questions.explanation: 航路によっては燃料の使用を最大20%減らせると述べている。

questions.question: What is one limitation of the sails?
choices: They can only be used on small ships.
questions.explanation: 取り付け費用が高く、強く安定した風の航路でしか最も効果がないとある。

title: Glass recycling problems
script: Narrator: Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality, so it may seem like an ideal material. In reality, however, much of the glass that people put in recycling bins is never recycled. One reason is that glass often breaks during collection and becomes mixed with other materials, making it difficult to sort. In addition, glass is heavy, so transporting it to recycling plants is expensive. To solve these problems, some towns now collect glass separately from other recyclables and have built recycling facilities closer to where people live.
translation: ガラスは品質を落とさずに何度でもリサイクルできるので、理想的な素材に思えるかもしれない。しかし実際には、人々がリサイクル箱に入れるガラスの多くはリサイクルされていない。理由の一つは、回収中にガラスが割れてほかの素材と混ざり、分別が難しくなることだ。さらにガラスは重いので、リサイクル工場へ運ぶ費用が高い。こうした問題を解決するため、一部の町ではほかの資源ごみと分けてガラスを回収し、住民の近くにリサイクル施設を建てている。

questions.question: Why is much glass not recycled?
choices: It loses quality each time it is recycled.
People rarely put glass in recycling bins.
It breaks and becomes mixed with other materials.
Recycling plants refuse to accept colored glass.
questions.explanation: 回収中に割れてほかの素材と混ざり分別が難しくなる、と説明されている。品質は落ちないとあるので2つ目は誤り。

questions.question: What have some towns done?
choices: Collected glass separately and built facilities nearby.
Asked people to reuse glass bottles at home.
Replaced glass bottles with plastic ones.
questions.explanation: ガラスを分けて回収し、住民の近くにリサイクル施設を建てたとある。

title: Paper straws
script: Narrator: To reduce plastic waste, many restaurants and cafés have replaced plastic straws with paper ones. While customers generally support the idea, many complain that paper straws become soft and fall apart in drinks. Some studies have also found that certain paper straws contain chemicals used to make them waterproof, which may not break down easily in the environment. As a result, some businesses are trying alternatives, such as straws made from rice or bamboo, while others have designed cups with lids that do not require straws at all.
translation: プラスチックごみを減らすため、多くのレストランやカフェがプラスチックのストローを紙のストローに替えた。客は概してこの考えを支持しているが、紙のストローは飲み物の中で柔らかくなって崩れると不満を言う人も多い。紙のストローの中には防水加工のための化学物質を含み、環境中で分解されにくいものがあるという研究もある。その結果、米や竹で作ったストローなどの代替品を試す店や、ストローがまったく要らないふた付きのカップを考案した店もある。

questions.question: What do many customers complain about?
choices: Paper straws become soft in drinks.
Plastic straws are no longer available anywhere.
Paper straws change the taste of drinks.
questions.explanation: 紙のストローは飲み物の中で柔らかくなって崩れると不満を言う人が多いとある。

questions.question: What have some businesses done?
choices: Asked customers to bring paper straws.
Designed lids that do not need straws.
questions.explanation: 米や竹のストローを試すほか、ストローが要らないふた付きカップを考案した店もあるとある。

title: Walking meetings
script: Narrator: Some companies have started holding walking meetings, in which employees discuss work while walking outside instead of sitting in a conference room. Supporters say that walking increases blood flow to the brain, which can make people more creative. A study at a university found that people produced more original ideas while walking than while sitting. Walking side by side may also make conversations feel less formal, helping employees speak more openly. However, walking meetings are not suitable for every situation, such as when people need to look at documents or take detailed notes.
translation: 会議室に座る代わりに、外を歩きながら仕事について話し合う「ウォーキング会議」を始めた企業がある。支持者によれば、歩くと脳への血流が増え、より創造的になれる。ある大学の研究では、人は座っているときより歩いているときのほうが独創的なアイデアを多く出した。並んで歩くことで会話が堅苦しくなくなり、従業員がより率直に話せるようになるかもしれない。しかし、書類を見たり詳しいメモを取ったりする必要があるときなど、ウォーキング会議がすべての場面に向いているわけではない。

questions.question: What did the university study find?
choices: People took better notes while walking.
Walking meetings were shorter than normal meetings.
People had more original ideas while walking.
Employees preferred meeting in conference rooms.
questions.explanation: 座っているときより歩いているときのほうが独創的なアイデアを多く出したとある。

questions.question: When are walking meetings unsuitable?
choices: When employees want to speak openly.
When only two people are meeting.
When people need to read documents.
questions.explanation: 最後に、書類を見たり詳しいメモを取ったりするときには向かないとある。

title: Tree planting controversy
script: Narrator: Planting trees is often promoted as a simple way to fight climate change, because trees absorb carbon dioxide as they grow. Many companies and governments have announced plans to plant millions or even billions of trees. However, some scientists warn that such projects can cause harm if they are not carefully planned. For example, planting trees on natural grasslands can destroy habitats for animals and plants that depend on open land. In addition, many young trees die because no one takes care of them after planting. Experts say that protecting existing forests is often more effective than planting new ones.
translation: 木は成長するにつれて二酸化炭素を吸収するので、植林は気候変動と戦う簡単な方法としてよく宣伝される。多くの企業や政府が何百万本、何十億本もの木を植える計画を発表している。しかし、慎重に計画しなければこうした事業は害をもたらしうると警告する科学者もいる。例えば、自然の草原に木を植えると、開けた土地に頼る動植物のすみかを壊してしまう。さらに、植えた後に世話をする人がいないため、多くの若木が枯れる。専門家によれば、新しい木を植えるより既存の森林を守るほうが効果的なことが多い。

questions.question: What problem can planting trees on grasslands cause?
choices: It can destroy habitats for some animals and plants.
It increases the amount of carbon dioxide.
It makes the soil too wet for farming.
questions.explanation: 自然の草原に木を植えると、開けた土地に頼る動植物のすみかを壊してしまうとある。

questions.question: What do experts say is often more effective?
choices: Cutting down old trees to plant new ones.
questions.explanation: 最後に、既存の森林を守るほうが効果的なことが多いと述べている。

title: Smart cities and privacy
script: Narrator: Around the world, cities are using sensors and data to improve public services. These so-called smart cities can adjust traffic lights based on the number of cars, monitor air pollution, and tell residents when the next bus will arrive. Supporters say that such technology can make cities more efficient and reduce energy use. However, critics are concerned about privacy. Cameras and sensors may collect large amounts of information about people's movements, and residents often do not know how this data is stored or used. Some cities have responded by creating clear rules about what data can be collected.
translation: 世界中の都市が、公共サービスを改善するためにセンサーやデータを活用している。こうした「スマートシティ」では、車の数に応じて信号を調整し、大気汚染を監視し、次のバスがいつ来るかを住民に知らせることができる。支持者は、こうした技術で都市がより効率的になりエネルギー使用も減ると言う。しかし批判する人はプライバシーを懸念している。カメラやセンサーは人々の移動について大量の情報を集める可能性があり、住民はそのデータがどう保存され使われるかを知らないことが多い。どのデータを集めてよいかについて明確な規則を作って対応した都市もある。

questions.question: What is one thing smart cities can do?
choices: Adjust traffic lights according to traffic.
Provide free buses for all residents.
Stop all air pollution in the city.
Reduce the number of cars to zero.
questions.explanation: 車の数に応じて信号を調整できると述べている。

questions.question: How have some cities responded to privacy concerns?
choices: By removing all cameras from the streets.
By selling residents' data to companies.
By making clear rules about data collection.
By stopping the use of sensors completely.
questions.explanation: 最後に、どのデータを集めてよいかについて明確な規則を作ったとある。

title: Real-Life: Train tickets
situation: You want to travel to Westford tomorrow morning and return the same evening. You want to spend as little money as possible. You hear the following announcement at the station.
script: Narrator: Attention, passengers. A one-way ticket to Westford costs twenty dollars, and a round-trip ticket costs thirty-five dollars. However, if you travel after nine thirty a.m. on weekdays, you can buy an off-peak round-trip ticket for just twenty-five dollars. Please note that off-peak tickets cannot be used on trains returning between five and seven p.m. Passengers who hold a rail card can also receive an additional ten percent discount on all tickets.
translation: 乗客の皆さまにお知らせします。ウェストフォードまでの片道切符は20ドル、往復切符は35ドルです。ただし平日の午前9時半以降にご乗車の場合は、オフピーク往復切符をわずか25ドルでお買い求めいただけます。オフピーク切符は午後5時から7時の間の帰りの列車ではご利用になれませんのでご注意ください。レールカードをお持ちの方は、すべての切符がさらに10%割引になります。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Buy an off-peak ticket and return after seven p.m.
Leave before nine thirty a.m. and return at six p.m.
questions.explanation: 最も安いのは25ドルのオフピーク往復切符。9時半以降に出発し、使えない午後5〜7時を避けて7時以降に帰れば同日往復できる。

title: Real-Life: Museum tour
situation: You are visiting a museum with your eight-year-old son. You want to join a guided tour that he will enjoy. You hear the following announcement.
script: Narrator: Welcome to the City History Museum. Today we are offering several guided tours. At eleven, there is a tour of our ancient pottery collection, which is recommended for adults with a strong interest in archaeology. At one o'clock, we have a family tour of the dinosaur hall, which includes hands-on activities for children aged six to twelve. At two thirty, there is a tour of our new photography exhibition. Tours are free, but please register at the information desk at least fifteen minutes before the start time.
translation: 市立歴史博物館へようこそ。本日はいくつかのガイドツアーをご用意しています。11時は古代の陶器コレクションのツアーで、考古学に強い関心のある大人の方におすすめです。1時は恐竜ホールのファミリーツアーで、6歳から12歳のお子さま向けの体験活動があります。2時半は新しい写真展のツアーです。ツアーは無料ですが、開始の15分前までに案内所でお申し込みください。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Go to the dinosaur hall at eleven.
Join the pottery tour at eleven.
Register for the photography tour by 2:15.
Register at the information desk by 12:45.
questions.explanation: 8歳の息子に合うのは6〜12歳向けの1時の恐竜ファミリーツアー。開始15分前までに案内所で申し込む必要があるので12時45分までに登録する。

title: Real-Life: Phone repair
situation: Your smartphone screen is cracked. You bought the phone eight months ago, and you need it back as soon as possible. You call the store and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Thank you for calling Mobile Plus. For screen repairs, we offer two options. If your phone is under one year old, the repair is covered by the manufacturer's warranty, but the phone must be sent to the service center, and the repair takes about one week. Alternatively, our in-store technicians can replace your screen within two hours for a fee of one hundred and twenty dollars. No appointment is necessary for in-store repairs; simply bring your phone to any of our branches.
translation: モバイルプラスにお電話いただきありがとうございます。画面の修理には2つの方法がございます。購入から1年未満の端末はメーカー保証で修理できますが、サービスセンターへの発送が必要で、修理に約1週間かかります。または、店内の技術者が120ドルの料金で2時間以内に画面を交換いたします。店内修理は予約不要です。お近くの支店に端末をお持ちください。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Take your phone to one of the store's branches.
Send your phone to the service center.
Make an appointment for an in-store repair.
questions.explanation: できるだけ早く必要なので、1週間かかる保証修理ではなく2時間で終わる店内修理を選ぶ。予約不要で支店に持ち込めばよい。

title: Real-Life: Apartment heating
situation: The heater in your apartment has stopped working. It is Saturday evening. You call the building management office and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: You have reached the management office of Greenview Apartments. Our office is open from nine to five, Monday through Friday. For general questions, please leave a message, and we will return your call on the next business day. If you are experiencing an emergency, such as a water leak, a gas smell, or a heating failure during the winter months, please call our twenty-four-hour maintenance line at 555-0199. For fire or medical emergencies, call 911 immediately.
translation: グリーンビュー・アパートメントの管理事務所です。事務所の受付時間は月曜から金曜の9時から5時です。一般的なお問い合わせはメッセージを残してください。翌営業日に折り返しお電話します。水漏れ、ガス臭、冬季の暖房の故障などの緊急の場合は、24時間対応の保守窓口 555-0199 にお電話ください。火災や急病の場合は、すぐに911に通報してください。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Leave a message for the management office.
Call the office again on Monday morning.
questions.explanation: 土曜の夜で事務所は閉まっているが、冬の暖房の故障は緊急扱いなので24時間対応の保守窓口に電話する。

title: Real-Life: Gym membership
situation: You want to join a gym. You can only exercise on weekends, and you want to use the swimming pool. You hear the following explanation from a staff member.
script: Narrator: We have four types of membership. The basic plan costs thirty dollars a month and allows you to use the gym equipment on weekdays only. The weekend plan costs twenty-five dollars and gives you access to the gym on Saturdays and Sundays, but it doesn't include the pool. The standard plan, at fifty dollars, includes the gym and pool every day. Finally, the premium plan, at seventy dollars, includes everything in the standard plan plus unlimited fitness classes.
translation: 会員には4種類あります。ベーシックプランは月30ドルで、平日のみジムの器具を使えます。週末プランは25ドルで土日にジムを使えますが、プールは含まれません。スタンダードプランは50ドルで、毎日ジムとプールを使えます。最後に、プレミアムプランは70ドルで、スタンダードの内容に加えてフィットネスクラスが受け放題です。

questions.question: Which plan should you choose?
questions.explanation: 週末にプールを使いたい。週末プランはプールなし、ベーシックは平日のみ。プールを含む最も安いのはスタンダードプラン。フィットネスクラスは必要ないのでプレミアムは不要。

title: Real-Life: Package delivery
situation: You missed a package delivery today. You will be at work tomorrow from eight a.m. to six p.m. You call the delivery company and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Thank you for calling Swift Delivery. If you missed a delivery, you have several options. We can try to deliver your package again tomorrow between nine a.m. and five p.m. If this time is not convenient, you can pick up your package at our local depot, which is open until nine p.m. on weekdays. You can also have the package sent to a convenience store near your home, but this service takes two additional days. To choose an option, please enter your tracking number now.
translation: スウィフト配送にお電話いただきありがとうございます。配達を受け取れなかった場合は、いくつかの方法がございます。明日の午前9時から午後5時の間に再配達できます。この時間が不都合な場合は、平日午後9時まで営業している地域の営業所でお受け取りいただけます。ご自宅近くのコンビニへの転送もできますが、この場合はさらに2日かかります。方法を選ぶには、追跡番号を入力してください。

questions.question: What should you do to get your package as soon as possible?
choices: Pick it up at the local depot after work tomorrow.
Have it sent to a convenience store.
Wait until the weekend for redelivery.
questions.explanation: 明日は8時から6時まで仕事なので9〜5時の再配達は受け取れない。コンビニ転送は2日余計にかかる。午後9時まで開いている営業所に仕事帰りに取りに行くのが最も早い。

title: Real-Life: Conference sessions
situation: You are attending a business conference. You want to learn about marketing on social media, and you must leave the conference by three p.m. You hear the following announcement.
script: Narrator: Good morning, everyone. Here are this afternoon's sessions. At one o'clock in Room A, Ms. Harris will speak about building a strong brand through traditional advertising. At the same time in Room B, there will be a panel discussion on international trade. At two o'clock in Room C, Mr. Patel will give a workshop on using social media to reach new customers. Please note that this workshop will last ninety minutes. The same social media workshop will be repeated tomorrow morning at ten in Room A.
translation: 皆さま、おはようございます。本日午後のセッションをご案内します。1時からA室で、ハリス氏が従来型広告による強いブランド作りについて講演します。同じ時間にB室では国際貿易に関するパネル討論があります。2時からC室で、パテル氏が新しい顧客を獲得するためのSNS活用ワークショップを行います。このワークショップは90分間ですのでご注意ください。同じSNSのワークショップは明日午前10時からA室でも行われます。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Go to Room C at two o'clock today.
Attend the workshop in Room A tomorrow morning.
Attend Ms. Harris's talk at one o'clock.
Join the panel discussion in Room B.
questions.explanation: SNSのワークショップは今日2時から90分で、3時までに出なければならないので最後まで受けられない。明日10時の同じワークショップに出ればよい。

title: Real-Life: Library books
situation: You borrowed three books from the library, and they are due today. You have finished two of them, but you want to keep the third one for another week. You hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Welcome to the Riverside Public Library information line. Books can be borrowed for two weeks. You can renew a book once for an additional two weeks, as long as no other member has reserved it. Renewals can be made online, by phone, or at the front desk. Please note that books that have been reserved by another member cannot be renewed and must be returned by the due date. Late returns are charged at fifty cents per book per day.
translation: リバーサイド公立図書館の案内電話です。本の貸出期間は2週間です。ほかの会員が予約していなければ、1回に限りさらに2週間延長できます。延長はオンライン、電話、カウンターで受け付けます。ほかの会員が予約している本は延長できず、返却期限までに返さなければなりませんのでご注意ください。返却が遅れた場合は1冊につき1日50セントかかります。

questions.question: What should you do first?
choices: Keep the book and pay the late fee.
Check whether the third book has been reserved by someone else.
Borrow the book again next week.
questions.explanation: 延長できるのはほかの会員が予約していない場合だけなので、まず3冊目が予約されていないか確認する必要がある。

title: Real-Life: Volunteer work
situation: You want to do volunteer work at an animal shelter. You are available on Saturday mornings, and you have no experience with animals. You hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Thank you for your interest in volunteering at Happy Paws Animal Shelter. We have several roles available. Dog walkers are needed on weekday afternoons, and previous experience with large dogs is required. Volunteers for our cat care team work on Saturday and Sunday mornings, and no experience is needed, but all new volunteers must attend a one-hour orientation session first. Orientation sessions are held on the first Saturday of every month. To sign up, please visit our website.
translation: ハッピーパウズ動物保護施設のボランティアにご関心をお寄せいただきありがとうございます。いくつかの役割がございます。犬の散歩係は平日の午後に募集しており、大型犬の扱いの経験が必要です。猫の世話チームのボランティアは土日の午前に活動し、経験は不要ですが、新しいボランティアは全員、まず1時間のオリエンテーションに参加しなければなりません。オリエンテーションは毎月第1土曜日に行われます。お申し込みはウェブサイトからどうぞ。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Apply to be a dog walker.
Go to the shelter next Saturday to care for cats.
Sign up for an orientation session on the website.
Gain experience with large dogs first.
questions.explanation: 土曜の午前に活動でき経験不要なのは猫の世話チーム。ただし新人はまずオリエンテーションに出る必要があり、申し込みはウェブサイトから。

title: Real-Life: Hotel check-out
situation: You are staying at a hotel. Your flight leaves at eight p.m., and you want to go sightseeing after checking out. You hear the following information from the front desk.
script: Narrator: Check-out time is eleven a.m. If you need a later check-out, we can extend it until two p.m. for an additional fee of thirty dollars, depending on availability. After checking out, guests are welcome to leave their luggage with us free of charge until midnight. We also offer an airport shuttle bus, which leaves from the front entrance every hour. The trip to the airport takes about forty-five minutes, so we recommend taking the bus at least three hours before your flight.
translation: チェックアウトは午前11時です。遅いチェックアウトをご希望の場合は、空き状況によって追加料金30ドルで午後2時まで延長できます。チェックアウト後は、深夜0時までお荷物を無料でお預かりします。また、正面玄関から1時間ごとに空港シャトルバスが出ています。空港まで約45分かかりますので、フライトの少なくとも3時間前のバスのご利用をおすすめします。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Pay for a late check-out until two p.m.
Take your luggage with you while sightseeing.
Leave your luggage at the hotel and take the shuttle by five p.m.
Take the shuttle bus at seven p.m.
questions.explanation: チェックアウト後に荷物を無料で預けて観光でき、8時の便の3時間前、つまり午後5時までにシャトルに乗ればよい。7時では遅すぎる。

title: Real-Life: Cooking class
situation: You want to take a cooking class to learn how to make healthy meals. You are a beginner and can only attend on weekday evenings. You hear the following information.
script: Narrator: Our cooking school offers several courses this month. On Tuesday evenings, we have an advanced French cuisine class for experienced cooks. On Wednesday evenings, there is a beginners' course called Healthy Home Cooking, which teaches simple, low-calorie recipes. On Saturday mornings, we offer a baking class for all levels. Please note that the Wednesday course is very popular and only has a few places left, so we recommend booking online as soon as possible.
translation: 当料理教室では今月いくつかのコースがございます。火曜の夜は経験者向けの上級フランス料理クラスです。水曜の夜は初心者向けの「ヘルシー家庭料理」コースで、簡単で低カロリーのレシピを教えます。土曜の午前はすべてのレベル向けのパン・お菓子作りクラスです。水曜のコースは大変人気で残りわずかですので、できるだけ早くオンラインでのご予約をおすすめします。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Sign up for the Tuesday evening class.
Visit the school on Wednesday to register.
Book the Wednesday course online soon.
questions.explanation: 初心者で平日の夜しか出られず健康的な料理を学びたいので水曜の夜のコース。残りわずかなので早くオンラインで予約する。

title: Real-Life: Bicycle rental
situation: You are visiting a city for one day and want to rent a bicycle for about five hours. You do not have a credit card. You hear the following explanation at a rental shop.
script: Narrator: We offer bicycles for rent by the hour or by the day. Hourly rentals cost five dollars per hour, and day rentals cost twenty dollars. All rentals require a deposit. If you pay by credit card, we just need to keep your card details. If you pay in cash, we ask for a fifty-dollar deposit, which will be returned when you bring the bicycle back. Please note that day rentals must be returned by six p.m. Helmets are available free of charge.
translation: 自転車は時間単位または1日単位でお貸ししています。時間貸しは1時間5ドル、1日貸しは20ドルです。すべてのレンタルに保証金が必要です。クレジットカードでお支払いの場合はカード情報をお預かりするだけです。現金でお支払いの場合は50ドルの保証金をお預かりし、自転車を返却したときにお返しします。1日貸しは午後6時までにご返却ください。ヘルメットは無料でお貸しします。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Pay five dollars per hour and give your card details.
Pay twenty dollars for a day rental and a fifty-dollar cash deposit.
Rent a bicycle for five hours with no deposit.
Pay twenty-five dollars for an hourly rental with no deposit.
questions.explanation: 5時間の時間貸しは25ドル、1日貸しは20ドルなので1日貸しが安い。カードがないので現金で50ドルの保証金を払う必要がある。

title: Real-Life: Doctor's appointment
situation: You have had a high fever since last night, and you want to see a doctor today. You call a clinic and hear the following message.
script: Narrator: Thank you for calling Maple Street Clinic. Our regular appointments are fully booked for this week. If you have a fever or cold symptoms, please do not come to the waiting room directly. Instead, we offer same-day online consultations with our doctors from two to five p.m. You can book these consultations through our website. If you have difficulty breathing or severe chest pain, please go to the emergency room at City Hospital.
translation: メープル通りクリニックにお電話いただきありがとうございます。今週の通常の予約はすべて埋まっております。発熱や風邪の症状がある方は、待合室に直接来ないでください。代わりに、午後2時から5時まで、医師による当日のオンライン診療を行っております。オンライン診療はウェブサイトから予約できます。呼吸が苦しい場合や激しい胸の痛みがある場合は、市立病院の救急外来に行ってください。

questions.question: What should you do?
choices: Go to the clinic's waiting room this afternoon.
Book an online consultation through the website.
Make a regular appointment for next week.
Go to the emergency room at City Hospital.
questions.explanation: 今日受診したいが通常予約は満員で、発熱があるので待合室に直接行ってはいけない。当日のオンライン診療をウェブサイトで予約する。呼吸困難などはないので救急は不要。

title: Part 2 Set 21
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: When is the quarterly report due?
Man: (A) By the end of next week.
Man: (B) It's a quarterly meeting.
Man: (C) Yes, I reported it.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Who's going to replace Ms. Carter while she's on leave?
Woman: (A) She'll leave at five.
Woman: (B) Someone from the Boston office.
Woman: (C) The lease expires in May.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Would you like a receipt?
Man: (A) Yes, please put it in the bag.
Man: (B) The recipe is online.
Man: (C) I received it yesterday.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Why is the parking garage closed today?
Woman: (A) They're repainting the lines.
Woman: (B) About two hundred cars.
Woman: (C) Close to the main entrance.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Have you met the new sales director?
Man: (A) Not yet, but I'm seeing her this afternoon.
Man: (B) The sales went up last month.
Man: (C) It's directly across the street.

questions.question: When is the quarterly report due?
choices: By the end of next week.
questions.explanation: 「四半期報告書の締め切りはいつですか」に「来週末までに」と時を答えている。quarterly の繰り返しや、reported の音を使った Yes の応答はひっかけ。

questions.question: Who's going to replace Ms. Carter while she's on leave?
questions.explanation: 「カーターさんの休職中、代わりは誰ですか」に「ボストン支社の人」と答えている。leave の別の意味(出発する)や、lease(leave と似た音)はひっかけ。

questions.question: Would you like a receipt?
choices: Yes, please put it in the bag.
questions.explanation: 「レシートは要りますか」に「はい、袋に入れてください」と応じている。recipe(receipt と似た音)、received の音のひっかけ。

questions.question: Why is the parking garage closed today?
questions.explanation: 「なぜ今日は駐車場が閉まっているのですか」に「線を塗り直しているから」と理由を答えている。台数や、close(近い)の別の意味はひっかけ。

questions.question: Have you met the new sales director?
choices: Not yet, but I'm seeing her this afternoon.
The sales went up last month.
questions.explanation: 「新しい営業部長に会いましたか」に「まだですが今日の午後会います」と答えている。sales の繰り返し、directly(director と似た音)はひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 22
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: Where should I leave these documents?
Man: (A) Leave at noon.
Man: (B) They're very important documents.
Man: (C) In the tray on my desk.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Is the cafeteria open on Saturdays?
Woman: (A) I'll have the chicken.
Woman: (B) Open the window, please.
Woman: (C) Only until two o'clock.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: How many people applied for the position?
Man: (A) Apply the cream twice a day.
Man: (B) It's a full-time position.
Man: (C) More than we expected.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Could you send me the slides from yesterday's presentation?
Woman: (A) She presented it very well.
Woman: (B) I'll e-mail them right after this meeting.
Woman: (C) The slide in the park is closed.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: Should we book the conference room or meet at the café?
Man: (A) I read that book last month.
Man: (B) The café would be more relaxing.
Man: (C) Yes, we should meet.

questions.question: Where should I leave these documents?
choices: In the tray on my desk.
questions.explanation: 「この書類をどこに置けばいいですか」に「私の机のトレーに」と場所を答えている。leave の別の意味、documents の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Is the cafeteria open on Saturdays?
questions.explanation: 「食堂は土曜日に開いていますか」に「2時までだけです」と答え、開いていることを示している。注文の言葉は cafeteria からの連想、open の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: How many people applied for the position?
choices: Apply the cream twice a day.
questions.explanation: 「その職に何人応募しましたか」に「予想より多く」と答えている。apply の別の意味(塗る)、position の繰り返しはひっかけ。

questions.question: Could you send me the slides from yesterday's presentation?
choices: I'll e-mail them right after this meeting.
The slide in the park is closed.
questions.explanation: 「昨日のプレゼンのスライドを送ってもらえますか」という依頼に「この会議の後すぐにメールします」と応じている。presented の音、slide(すべり台)の別の意味はひっかけ。

questions.question: Should we book the conference room or meet at the café?
choices: I read that book last month.
The café would be more relaxing.
questions.explanation: 選択疑問文に「カフェのほうがくつろげる」と一方を選んでいる。book(本)の別の意味、Yes で始まる応答はひっかけ。

title: Part 2 Set 23
script:
Narrator: Number 1.
Woman: What time does the store close tonight?
Man: (A) It's close to the bank.
Man: (B) At nine, as usual.
Man: (C) Yes, I'm closing the store.
Narrator: Number 2.
Man: Didn't the client approve the design?
Woman: (A) The sign is on the door.
Woman: (B) Yes, I'm the client.
Woman: (C) She asked for a few small changes.
Narrator: Number 3.
Woman: Who should I talk to about my paycheck?
Man: (A) I'll check the pay phone.
Man: (B) Talk to you later.
Man: (C) Someone in the payroll office.
Narrator: Number 4.
Man: Let's take a short break before we continue.
Woman: (A) The brakes were repaired.
Woman: (B) Good idea—I need some coffee.
Woman: (C) Continue straight ahead.
Narrator: Number 5.
Woman: How far is the hotel from the airport?
Man: (A) About twenty minutes by taxi.
Man: (B) It's far better than the old one.
